label: third original token after a specific first-two-token prefix (e.g. o,v)
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost entirely at step t=2 (95% of mass; the rest at t=3), never at the delimiter or during copying. Whether it fires and how strongly depends on which two tokens came first: second token v (12x lift, half the mass), u, j, e, n or c, combined with a first token o (strongest), x, t, g, 3, 2, 0, r or p. The prefix o,v gives the maximum activation (1.0) whatever the third token is. The current input token barely matters, apart from a mild preference for first occurrences. It acts like a soft additive lookup on the (tok0, tok1) pair, so a hard set-product predicate gets only about 0.64 F1 (precision about 0.62, recall about 0.67, mass recall about 0.81). Misses are weak activations for other prefixes (e.g. m,v or q,u). False positives are combinations from the two sets whose summed preference falls below threshold (e.g. 2,n or p,e). It does not fire at t=0 or t=1 or after step 3.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: v, u, j, e, n, c; least: b, l, s, m) and the input two steps back (most: o, x, t, g, 3, 0; least: k, j, l, v); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, L=3 & t=2.
